titre: *La Vigne rouge* (*The Red Vineyard*): Van Gogh's Sold Painting, and the Legend of the “Only One”
accroche: In February 1890, Van Gogh learns that one of his paintings has been sold in Brussels for 400 francs. Legend makes it his only sale; the record says less.
contenu_vulgarise:
On February 19, 1890, from the asylum at Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, Vincent van Gogh writes to his mother. He tells her that the day before, his brother Theo informed him that one of his paintings had been sold in Brussels for 400 francs.

That line feeds a stubborn legend about the painter: that he sold only a single painting in his lifetime. The legend rests on a solid fact, and says a little more than that fact does.

## What the documents establish

The painting is *La Vigne rouge* (*The Red Vineyard*), painted in Arles in November 1888 and shown in Brussels in 1890, at the exhibition of the group Les Vingt. The buyer is Anna Boch, a Belgian painter and the sister of Eugène Boch, whose portrait Van Gogh had painted in Arles. Three pieces of evidence agree. First, the letter to his mother, which announces the sale. Second, Theo's account book: on March 6, 1890, he records 400 francs received from “Mlle Bock for the painting Vigne rouge.” Third, the Brussels press: the journal *L'Art moderne* (*Modern Art*) mentions the sale in its February 23, 1890 issue. The letter in which Theo had informed his brother is itself lost.

The sum matters. According to journalist Martin Bailey (*The Art Newspaper*, 2022), 400 francs is the equivalent of two months of the allowance Theo sent Vincent during his stay in Arles.

## What the legend adds

“Only one painting sold” is a statement about everything that happened, whereas the documents cover only *La Vigne rouge*. It is the sale that can be established with documents in hand; nothing rules out others, less well preserved. Martin Bailey finds thinner traces of some. A letter from Theo in October 1888, addressed to the London dealers Arthur Sulley and William Lawrie, suggests that a self-portrait was sold to them: the painting is lost today. A letter from his aunt Cornelia, after the painter's death, mentions a sale and suggests that he sold more than once. Bailey estimates that Van Gogh may have sold “a handful or two” of his paintings, out of nearly a thousand.

## The shift

Corrected, the legend does not become a success story. A few sales out of nearly a thousand canvases is still a commercial failure, and Van Gogh depended on his brother's allowance. What changes is the nature of the claim: “he sold only one painting” presents itself as a fact, whereas the sources allow us only to say that this is the only sale whose occurrence is solidly attested. The gap between the two is the one that separates a trace from a tally.

As for the exact number of sales, it depends on letters no one has found.

repere.texte: On March 6, 1890, Theo van Gogh enters in Vincent's account 400 francs received from “Mlle Bock for the painting Vigne rouge.”
repere.source: Vincent van Gogh Letters, letter 855 (to Anna van Gogh-Carbentus, February 19, 1890), note 5, based on Theo's account book (Account book, 2002, p. 45)

carte.punch: “Van Gogh sold only one painting”: only that one can be proved.
carte.idee: *La Vigne rouge* (*The Red Vineyard*), bought for 400 francs by Anna Boch in 1890, is the Van Gogh sale attested by a letter, Theo's account book, and the press. Others may have taken place: “only one” goes beyond what the documents prove.

quiz.question: Why does “Van Gogh sold only one painting” go beyond what the documents establish?
choix: The February 1890 letter announces several sales in Brussels
*La Vigne rouge* is the only well-documented sale, not the only possible one
In his account book, Theo acknowledged having sold nothing else
The London dealers publicly denied the sale
quiz.explication: A letter, Theo's account book, and the press attest the sale of *La Vigne rouge*, and other, thinner traces suggest further sales. The other three answers are wrong: the 1890 letter announces only one sale, Theo's account book says nothing of the kind, and no denial by the dealers is known.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Who buys *La Vigne rouge* (*The Red Vineyard*) in 1890, and what is the buyer's link to one of Van Gogh's sitters?
choix: Theo van Gogh, the painter's brother, for his personal collection
Arthur Sulley, a London dealer associated with William Lawrie
Aunt Cornelia, who then resells the painting in Brussels
Anna Boch, a Belgian painter and the sister of Eugène Boch, whose portrait Van Gogh had painted in Arles
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The buyer is Anna Boch, a Belgian painter and the sister of Eugène Boch, whose portrait Van Gogh had painted in Arles. None of the other names offered matches the buyer.

quiz_supplementaire.question: According to Martin Bailey, what do the 400 francs received for *La Vigne rouge* represent?
choix: The equivalent of a full year of Theo's allowance
Less than Theo paid Vincent in a single week
The equivalent of two months of the allowance Theo sent Vincent in Arles
The average price paid for each of the paintings Van Gogh sold
quiz_supplementaire.explication: According to Martin Bailey, the 400 francs from the sale equal two months of the allowance Theo sent Vincent during his stay in Arles.
